quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they will distract you.
Should be avoided since other drivers will see you easily.
Are only recommended in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often for safety. You need to know what is behind you at all times.

questions.question: Which types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel. The front brake is stronger.

questions.question: To lessen the chances of being in an accident, you should:

options.text: Not use your headlight during the day.
Communicate your intentions to other drivers.
Only use one portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers what you plan to do. Use your signals, brake lights, and lane position. Stay aware of traffic around you and be ready to avoid hazards.

questions.question: If only one alcoholic drink is consumed:

options.text: Judgment and riding abilities can still be affected.
There is usually no effect on the body.
There is an effect on the body, but it only lasts for a short time.
There is an effect on the body, but it can be eliminated by drinking coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and riding abilities can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your judgment and riding ability. Only your body can remove alcohol over time. Coffee does not help.

questions.question: Which of the following does not need to be checked regularly?
questions.explanation: Check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes before every ride. Small mechanical problems can be dangerous.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, be sure you can:

options.text: See the lane behind you and the lane next to you.
See only the lane behind you.
See only the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirror to see the lane behind you and the lane to the side of you. The road is more important than seeing your arm or shoulder.

questions.question: For the best protection, riding gloves should be made of:
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another tough material for proper protection.

questions.question: When conducting a pre-ride check, be sure that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes cause some friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before every ride. Each one should feel firm and hold the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe since there is so much traffic there.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous for motorcyclists because many accidents happen there when other drivers cross paths with riders.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Wind noise while riding can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: If you think your motorcycle will take longer to stop than usual, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance on slippery surfaces. If your motorcycle needs more time to stop, stay farther back from the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect the face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield protects your eyes and face the best. Regular eyeglasses or sunglasses do not provide enough protection. In Vermont, you don't need eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist constantly watch for ahead on the road?
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead to see changing traffic, hazards, and ways to escape danger. Be ready to react quickly to any changes.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How should you handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to get away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate at a faster speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When should a rider check their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, at intersections, when changing lanes, and when turning.

questions.question: What kind of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that tell you the rules, like speed limits, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow what these signs say.

questions.question: Can motorcyclists share lanes with cars or other non-motorcycle vehicles?

options.text: Yes, but it is not recommended.
Yes, if there is heavy traffic.
Yes, if the road is dry.
No, motorcyclists cannot share a lane with non-motorcycle vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, motorcyclists cannot share a lane with non-motorcycle vehicles.
questions.explanation: In Nevada, motorcyclists cannot ride in the same lane as another vehicle, pass another vehicle in the same lane, or ride between vehicles in other lanes, even if those vehicles are stopped. Two motorcycles can ride side by side in the same lane, but this is not recommended.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Keep your hands near the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands near the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, keep your hands ready near the clutch and brakes. This lets you react faster if you need to stop or avoid danger.

questions.question: What is one benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance?

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a long time.
Maintenance checks help prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: Regular maintenance keeps your motorcycle running like new. Make inspections part of your regular maintenance routine.

questions.question: How important are signals on a motorcycle?

options.text: They are more important than signals on cars and trucks.
You should only use them when another vehicle is right next to you.
They are less important than signals on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more important than signals on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders are more at risk than car and truck drivers. For this reason, using signals is even more important for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders should wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: What material are motorcycle riding gloves usually made from?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Which of these should you NOT check on your tires before riding?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire air pressure, general wear, and tread. You do not need to check flexibility.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It lets you see clearly to the sides.
It has no markings or labels.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets you see clearly to the sides.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet allows you to see clearly to the sides as needed for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels and markings with the maker's name, instructions, and safety standard information.
